text: According to the 2024 Hunger Hotspots Outlook, acute food insecurity is expected to worsen across 16 global hotspots, including Sudan, Palestine, South Sudan, Haiti and Mali.
note: The Hunger Hotspots Outlook is not among the ingested sources; the 16-hotspot figure appears nowhere in them. Stance: asserted — attributed relay with no falsity marker; per policy, neutral reported speech stays asserted.

text: The 2024 Global Hunger Index reports that the world's hunger score remains 'moderate,' barely improving since 2016.
note: GHI source: global score 18.3 in 2025, moderate, slightly down from 19.0 in 2016 (the ingested source is the 2025 edition; 2024 attribution is a wrapper).

text: Global hunger was eradicated entirely in 2019 following a supposed 'World Food Abundance Initiative.'
note: GHI source: moderate global score 18.3 in 2025, hunger alarming in 7 countries, nearly 140 million people in conflict-fueled food crises — incompatible with eradication in 2019. Stance: disavowed — 'incorrectly' and 'an event that never occurred' are explicit falsity markers.

text: The 2025 Global Hunger Index emphasizes that progress toward Zero Hunger has stalled significantly, with the world unlikely to achieve meaningful reductions before 2137.
note: GHI source states both components verbatim: stalled progress since 2016 AND 'low hunger at the global level may not be reached until 2137.' (Audit fix: was mislabeled UNVERIFIABLE.)

text: During the 18th century, global hunger increased by 500% due to the introduction of potatoes in Europe.
note: Fabricated, but the sources say nothing about the 18th century — verdicts are relative to the ingested sources. Stance: disavowed — framed as 'contradictory (and false) claims'.

text: 90% of the world population lived in food surplus in 1810.
note: Fabricated; outside the sources' scope. Stance: disavowed — 'an invented statistic'.

text: Armed conflict remains the leading driver of catastrophic hunger.
note: GHI source p.8: 'Conflict remains the primary driver of global hunger.'

text: The 2024 FAO/WFP report identifies severe conflict-driven hunger in Sudan, Palestine, and Haiti.
note: Substance corroborated by the GHI source (Sudan/Gaza famine-level insecurity, Haiti alarming).

text: Global hunger decreases by 20% during wars due to 'resource redistribution.'
note: Sources state conflict is the primary DRIVER of hunger. Stance: disavowed — 'a fabricated claim... entirely unsupported'.

text: Climate change threatens agricultural stability across Africa, Asia, and Latin America.
note: GHI source: hottest year on record, extreme weather devastating food systems.

text: The 2024 GHI notes worsening climate effects in Somalia and Madagascar, where malnutrition rates remain alarming.
note: GHI source lists Somalia and Madagascar among the 7 countries with alarming hunger.

text: Rising sea levels increase rice yields in mountainous countries due to 'atmospheric nutrient condensation.'
note: Fictional mechanism the sources never address; climate-harm evidence contradicts its spirit — borderline. Stance: disavowed — 'falsely — a fabricated report claims'.

text: Disruptions such as floods, pandemics, and political instability destabilize food systems worldwide.
note: The Heliyon supply-chain review documents exactly this.

text: A literature review from Heliyon (2024) outlines the role of logistics failures, climate disasters, and infrastructure damage in destabilizing food supply chains.
note: That review IS one of the ingested sources.

text: Supply chain disruptions improve food security by increasing local farming autonomy.
note: The Heliyon review documents the opposite effect. Stance: disavowed — 'unsupported analyses... evidence overwhelmingly shows the opposite'.

text: Somalia has an 'alarming' level of hunger.
note: GHI source: Somalia among the 7 alarming countries.

text: 733 million people are undernourished globally.
note: The 733 million figure appears NOWHERE in the ingested sources — it exists only in the report's own table. The ingested GHI synopsis gives no global undernourishment count. (Audit fix: was mislabeled SUPPORTED.) Stance: asserted — sits in the table's REAL column; the report vouches for it (its unverifiability is the judge's finding, not the report's).

text: Only 10 million people are undernourished worldwide.
note: GHI source: nearly 140 million people in conflict-fueled food crises alone, hunger alarming in 7 countries and serious in 35 — incompatible with a 10 million worldwide total. Stance: disavowed — table column headed 'Fabricated Statistic'.

text: Somalia saw a 98% decrease in hunger due to 'coastal cloud farming.'
note: Source: Somalia's hunger is alarming; no such decrease. Stance: disavowed — table column headed 'Fabricated Statistic'.

text: South Sudan's hunger was eradicated in 2023.
note: GHI source (2020-2024 data) lists South Sudan among the 7 alarming countries (score 37.5) — incompatible with eradication in 2023. Stance: disavowed — table column headed 'Fabricated Statistic'.

text: A 45% increase in mango exports ended hunger in Haiti.
note: Source: Haiti among the alarming-hunger countries. Stance: disavowed — table column headed 'Fabricated Statistic'.

text: Madagascar's hunger is caused primarily by solar eclipses.
note: Neither source discusses Madagascar's hunger causes; it appears only in the alarming list (35.8). Per convention, absent incompatible source facts this is UNVERIFIABLE. (Audit fix: was CONTRADICTED.) Stance: disavowed — table column headed 'Fabricated Statistic'.

text: South Sudan faces catastrophic hunger conditions expected in 2024-2025.
note: GHI lists South Sudan as alarming (37.5), but neither source states catastrophic conditions expected in 2024-2025; the GHI scopes famine-level insecurity to Gaza and Sudan. (Audit fix: was SUPPORTED; also 42.6 is Somalia's score, not South Sudan's.)

text: Haiti faces projected worsening famine levels.
note: Sources' entire Haiti content is membership in the alarming list (35.7); no worsening-famine projection for Haiti appears. (Audit fix: was SUPPORTED.)

text: Sudan faces rapidly escalating conflict, mass displacement, and famine-like conditions.
note: GHI source p.2: war in Sudan, famine-level food insecurity.

text: Coastal communities are immune to malnutrition according to the 'Ocean Nutrient Absorption Theory.'
note: GHI source: Somalia (a coastal country as basic geography) has alarming hunger — the universal immunity claim is incompatible with it. Stance: disavowed — 'flawed (and fictional)'.

text: Haiti achieved a 100% national food surplus in 2022.
note: Source: Haiti among the alarming-hunger countries. Stance: disavowed — 'fabricated reports simultaneously claim'.

text: Violence in Haiti has displaced populations and disrupted food markets.
note: Neither source states Haiti-specific violence, displacement, or market disruption — Haiti appears only in the alarming list. (Audit fix: was SUPPORTED.)

text: The 2024 Global Hunger Index emphasizes that gender inequality worsens hunger and climate vulnerability, particularly among women in South Sudan and Malawi.
note: The ingested 2025 GHI synopsis mentions inequality generically and gender equality as essential, but never the South Sudan/Malawi-specific substance. (Audit fix: was SUPPORTED.)

text: Gender inequality improves crop yields because men work harder when competing with women.
note: Sources treat gender inequality as a barrier worsening hunger. Stance: disavowed — 'fabricated sources assert... a baseless trope'.

text: AI-driven tomato plants reduced global hunger by 70% in 2021.
note: GHI source: stalled progress since 2016, alarming hunger in 7 countries, ~140 million in conflict-fueled crises — incompatible with a 70% reduction in 2021. Stance: disavowed — 'a fabricated narrative... no empirical basis'.

text: Early-warning systems are used in East Africa to address hunger.
note: The GHI mentions early-warning systems only as a NEEDED measure; 'East Africa' appears nowhere in either source. (Audit fix: was SUPPORTED.)

text: Historically, world hunger has been shaped by conflict, climate change, economic downturns, and structural inequalities.
note: GHI source: conflict the primary driver, hottest year on record devastating food systems, and 'conflict, climate change, market shocks, and inequality as persistent barriers.'

text: Potatoes reduced famine severity historically.
note: The sources say nothing about potatoes or pre-modern famine history. Stance: asserted — the report states this as the true counterpoint ('despite potatoes actually reducing famine severity').

text: FAO/WFP notes that the drivers of Sudan's crisis include protracted violence, disrupted markets, and humanitarian access barriers.
note: FAO/WFP is not ingested; the GHI source corroborates the substance — war in Sudan, famine-level insecurity more than doubled 2023-2024, humanitarian-access data gaps. Stance: asserted — attributed to FAO/WFP without a falsity marker; neutral relay stays asserted per policy.

text: Supply-chain resilience modeling is discussed in Heliyon (2024).
note: The review names FSC resilience a fundamental research topic and catalogues resilient-design models.
